name: Niuafoʻou
note: Island: the northernmost island of Tonga, a volcanic rim island with a crater lake, reached by air. Named by Tonga Tourism and TongaPocketGuide as a hiking and lake destination; a separate island-level destination or standalone.

name: Niuatoputapu
note: Island: volcanic island of The Niuas, 240 km north of Vavaʻu with white beaches, reef diving and village life, reached by weekly flight from Vavaʻu. Island-level destination or standalone.

name: Tafahi
note: Island: small volcanic island 9 km north-north-east of Niuatoputapu, with a 546-656 m stratovolcano climbed with a local guide (view to Samoa) and one village; boats from Falehau Wharf.

name: Vai Lahi
note: Crater lake: large freshwater crater lake (4 km wide, 84 m deep) in the Niuafoʻou caldera, with four islands; vantage points reached via locals.

name: Vai Siʻi
note: Crater lake: smaller soda lake beside Vai Lahi, separated by sand hills; no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Niuafoʻou Caldera
note: Birdwatching area: the central caldera where the endangered Tongan megapode is most often seen, reached on foot with locals. No own Wikipedia article: the island's article is not its page, so views are 0.

name: Futu Wharf
note: Gateway: the only landing place on Niuafoʻou, at the end of a lava flow in Futu; boat trips depart here, not a draw in itself.

name: Niuafoʻou Lava Fields
note: Natural feature: lava flows from the 1929-1946 eruptions still visible across the island; Wikivoyage mentions them only in its background text. No own Wikipedia article: the island's article is not its page, so views are 0.

name: Mokotu
note: Natural feature: 250 m high point on the Niuafoʻou crater rim; named only in the island's Wikipedia article.

name: Hihifo Spring
note: Natural feature: a crystal clear freshwater spring in a small pool in Hihifo village on Niuatoputapu, with steps down for swimming.

name: Niuatoputapu Highest Point
note: Hill: 157 m highest point of Niuatoputapu behind Hihifo and Falehauʻou, a guided steady climb with views over the island and to Tafahi.

name: Niuatoputapu White Sand Beaches
note: Beaches: long stretches of white sand around the east, south and west rims of Niuatoputapu, best on the north-west side; a stretch of beaches, not one named beach.

name: Niuatoputapu Reefs
note: Dive and snorkel site: healthy, unspoiled outer reef around Niuatoputapu with no rentals on the island, so visitors need their own gear and a boat or calm day.

name: Niuatoputapu Shipwreck
note: Dive site: a shipwreck on one of the outer reefs of Niuatoputapu, which a local must show the way to; it has no formal name in the sources.

name: Falehau Wharf
note: Gateway: wharf on Niuatoputapu's north coast where local fishermen's boats leave for Tafahi, not a draw in itself.

name: Hihifo
note: Village: the largest village of The Niuas, with the government offices, post office and police on Niuatoputapu; base for the spring and the hill climb.

name: Vaipoa
coordinates_source: OSM place=hamlet 'Vaipoa' via resolve-pin (MEDIUM); the Wikipedia point is the island's
note: Village: the middle village of Niuatoputapu, by the spot where boats leave for Tafahi, with a Sunday church service open to visitors.

name: Falehau
coordinates_source: OSM place=hamlet 'Falehau' via resolve-pin (HIGH: Commons geotag within 800 m)
note: Village: village on Niuatoputapu's north-west harbour, where boats leave for Tafahi; a Sunday church service is open to visitors.
